THE LEARNED SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC GANGAVATHI IN E.P.NO.152/2012, BY ALLOWING THIS C.R.P IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND ETC.,
 THESE PETITIONS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -4-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7620  CRP No. 100025 of 2016  C/W CRP No. 100023 of 2016  ORDER 1.

The petitioners - land losers are before this Court in these two petitions aggrieved by the orders dated 12.08.2024 passed in the E.P. Nos. 94/2013 & 152/2012.
2.

The aforesaid execution petitions in E.P. Nos. 94/2013 & 152/2012 were filed by the petitioners - land losers seeking interest in terms of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Sunder Vs.
Union of India1.

Accepting the contentions of the petitioners - land losers, the Executing Court has made the calculation as per paragraph No.17 of the impugned order and has held that the petitioners - land losers are entitled for the interest of Rs.6,51,223/- i.e., accrued on the compensation till 20.08.1998 in E.P. No.94/2013 and interest of Rs.6,50,317/- i.e., accrued on the compensation in till 20.08.1998 in E.P. No.152/2012.
These orders are put in question by the petitioners - land losers.
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the Executing Court committed grave error in not granting the interest till the date of payment.
He further submits that there is no justification in the Executing Court limiting the payment of interest only up to the date of 20.08.1998 and no reason is assigned in that regard.

He submits that the interest calculated is payable in terms of the statutory provisions contained under the Land Acquisition Act as such until and unless the entire compensation amount is not paid, the petitioners - land losers are entitled for the interest till such date.
4.

In response, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 - beneficiary submits that the entire compensation amount has been paid and satisfied as on 20.01.2000 as such question of payment of further interest would not arise.
He, however, submits that the calculation made by the Executing Court appears to be on an incorrect basis, which require reconsideration.
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and perused the records.

6. There cannot be any dispute with regard to the fact that in terms of the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, more particularly Sections 23, 28 & 34 of the Land Acquisition Act, the components of the compensation include the determined market value of the property, solecism and the interest Sri.Hire Yallappa vs The Assistant Commissioner on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82479437/
4 and all statutory benefits incidental thereof, and the calculation of interest would run up to the payment and satisfaction of the entire compensation amount.
7.

sentences.text: The Executing Court, while making calculation though, has upheld the rights of the petitioners - land losers to their claim of interest, but for the reason best known, has limited the said calculation of interest only till the 20.08.1998.

It is also necessary to note here that, as per the submissions of the learned counsel appearing for the beneficiary, the entire compensation amount was paid NC:
2024:KHC-D:7620 as on 20.08.1998 and the execution filed in this regard was closed, having been satisfied on the 20.01.2000.
8.
After hearing the learned counsel appearing for the parties and on perusal of the records, it is clear that there seem to be an anomaly in the calculation made and arrived at by the Executing Court.
The order is not clear as to on what basis, a sum of Rs.6,51,223/- is arrived at and the basis on which the said amount is restricted only up to 20.08.1998.

If the compensation as payable under the statute is not paid even as on the date of passing of the impugned order, nothing prevented the Executing Court to make it clear whether the petitioners were entitled for the interest till disposal or till payment of the amount.

If, on the other hand, as contended by the learned counsel appearing for the beneficiary, the compensation amount had been paid and satisfied as on the 20.08.1998, what was the reason for the Executing Court to award the compensation of interest thereof.
In that view of the matter, this Court is of the considered view that the impugned orders be set aside and the matters be remanded to the Executing Court.
The parties shall be given an opportunity to furnish their calculations and thereafter pass an order with reference to the relevant provisions of law applicable in the matter.
Such calculations and the order shall be passed within an outer limit of six (6) months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
10. The petitions are allowed accordingly.
